components.cost_effect: n+1 shifted population locations; actual sampling cost is charged by the batch component.
components.goal: Separate deterministic derivative approximation error from stochastic error.
components.key_estimate: Exactness cancels polynomial terms except the derivative; summing remainder norms yields ||Z-J_y grad g[v]||<=W*A_r*h^(r+1)=n*A_r*h^r=a. Substitution gives W=n^(1+1/r)*Mbar^(1/r)*(Lambdabar*V)^(1+1/r)*((r+1)!)^((beta-1)/r)*a^(-1/r). Since ((r+1)!)^(1/r) is bounded above and below by constant multiples of r and r<=n<=r+1, this is <=C_beta*r^beta*a^(-1/r), using the lower factorial bound when beta<1.
components.name: Taylor remainder and exact stencil
components.operation: Use the complete odd Chebyshev stencil and h=(a/(n*A_r))^(1/r).
components.requires: Degree-r lower-variable Taylor remainder bounded by A_r*|t|^(r+1), globally for ||v||<=V.
transfer_checks: A qualitative smoothness label cannot replace the quantitative Taylor remainder.
Changing nodes or restricting the allowed radius requires a new bias and W analysis.

components.cost_effect: Ceiling overhead at most n+1 beyond B; no shared-sample cancellation is used.
components.goal: Control variance without an additional multiplicative node-count factor.
components.key_estimate: Conditional expectation is the discrete difference. Independence cancels cross terms, so E||Zhat-Z||^2<=sigma^2 sum_j d_j^2/b_j<=sigma^2 sum_j |d_j|*W/B=sigma^2 W^2/B. Also ceil(u)<=u+1 gives sum_j b_j<=B+n+1. Node means are summed deterministically rather than sampled as random nodes, so no bound on their magnitudes is needed.
components.name: Absolute-weight allocation
components.operation: Use independent node means with b_j=ceil(B*|d_j|/W).
components.requires: Conditionally independent centered gradient noises with second moment<=sigma^2; each nonzero weight receives at least one sample.
transfer_checks: Reusing the same sample across nodes changes the covariance argument.
Unbiasedness is for Z, not for the actual derivative; keep the bias term a.

limitations.statement: Generally biased for the actual population derivative; exact conditional unbiasedness concerns only the discrete difference.
This record is a local derivative estimator. It does not output a stationary point or establish the full minimax upper bound without the inner, adjoint and outer procedures in Appendix B.
For beta<1 the radius can grow with order. Restricted query domains or bounded-radius permissions require new checks.

content.local_verification: Bias, factorial-weight scaling, conditional variance and ceiling accounting are expanded in the components for independent checking; no independent Reviewer check is asserted.

variants.cost: Exactly sum_j b_j raw g-gradient samples, bounded by B+n+1. Every endpoint, node and batch sample is charged. No sample is reused at another node. This component incurs no f-gradient calls.
variants.name: Weighted independent-node estimator
variants.output: A vector Zhat_B in R^{d_x+d_y}. Conditionally on the input/history, E Zhat_B=Z_{r,h}, ||Z_{r,h}-J_y grad g(x,y)[v]||<=a and E||Zhat_B-Z_{r,h}||^2<=sigma^2*W^2/B. Here J_y grad g[v]=(g_xy*v,g_yy*v), and W<=C_beta*r^beta*a^(-1/r), with C_beta depending on fixed envelope parameters, L_2 and V, not r.
public_inputs: Finite dimensions, x,y and v with ||v||<=V; V>=max(1,L_0/mu).
Available integer order 1<=r<=p, quantitative bounds M,Lambda_s>0,beta>=0, baseline L_2, target bias 0<a<1 and allocation parameter B>=1.
variants.query_and_update: Allocate b_j=ceil(B*|d_j|/W) samples to (x,y+h*t_j*v). Obtain each sample once using the fresh g-gradient oracle, and form its node mean Gbar_j. Output Zhat_B=sum_{j=0}^n d_j*Gbar_j. The mathematical discrete difference is Z_{r,h}=sum_j d_j*grad g(x,y+h*t_j*v); it is not an oracle response.
variants.requirements: Global population derivative assumptions from Section 2: g_xy,g_yy jointly L_2-Lipschitz, and for r>=2 the stated lower-variable top Lipschitz bounds yielding the degree-r Taylor remainder. A fixed envelope L_j=M*Lambda_s^j*(j!)^beta for j>=3 is required for the order-uniform W bound. Fresh full g-gradient samples are conditionally unbiased with variance<=sigma^2 at every shifted real query. All samples within and across nodes are independent, conditionally on the fixed inputs. No samplewise smoothness, common random numbers, HVP feedback or deterministic gradient-size bound is assumed.
variants.state_and_initialization: Fix the query and direction conditionally on the past. Let n be the smallest odd integer >=r, so r<=n<=r+1. For j=0,...,n let t_j=cos(j*pi/n), c_0=c_n=2 and other c_j=1, s_n=(-1)^((n-1)/2). Choose fixed Mbar>=max(1,M,sqrt(2)*L_2), Lambdabar>=max(1,Lambda_s). Set A_r=Mbar*(Lambdabar*V)^(r+1)*((r+1)!)^(beta-1), h=(a/(n*A_r))^(1/r), d_j=s_n*(-1)^j/(n*h*c_j*t_j^2), W=sum_j|d_j|=n/h.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: All node counts are fixed by the public inputs before the samples are observed. Stop after all b_j samples have been obtained. The radius is not capped by strong convexity because these are direct real lower-variable queries, not solutions to negatively perturbed objectives.

use_restrictions: Component only; do not promote its cost to a full optimization guarantee.
Complete local bias, variance and ceiling arguments must be independently checked by the Reviewer.
Batch revisions and the uses link are for runner prepare; no acceptance or publication is claimed.

links.note: Exact polynomial differentiation and W=n/h; this is a stencil dependency, not an end-to-end performance link.

summary: A local estimator of J_y grad g(x,y)[v] with controlled deterministic bias, independent-sampling variance and fully charged node batches; not an end-to-end optimizer.
title: Independent fresh-gradient Chebyshev derivative estimator component
use_when: Approximate a lower-variable population-gradient derivative using fresh independent gradients at shifted nodes.
